claims.claim: mounts a remote as a FUSE filesystem on Linux, FreeBSD, macOS and Windows
claims.evidence_quote: Rclone mount allows Linux, FreeBSD, macOS and Windows to mount any of Rclone's cloud storage systems as a file system with FUSE.

claims.claim: The mountpoint must be an existing empty directory on Unix
claims.evidence_quote: On Linux/macOS/FreeBSD start the mount like this, where /path/to/local/mount is an empty existing directory

claims.claim: It runs in the foreground by default
claims.evidence_quote: Mount runs in foreground mode by default. Use the --daemon flag to force background mode.

claims.claim: stops on Ctrl-C, SIGINT or SIGTERM
claims.evidence_quote: When the program ends while in foreground mode, either via Ctrl+C or receiving a SIGINT or SIGTERM signal, the mount should be automatically stopped.

claims.claim: `--daemon` backgrounds it on Unix and then you unmount manually with `fusermount -u` (or `fusermount3 -u`)
claims.evidence_quote: When running in background mode the user will have to stop the mount manually: # Linux fusermount -u /path/to/local/mount # ... or on some systems fusermount3 -u /path/to/local/mount

claims.claim: With `--daemon`, the parent waits up to `--daemon-wait` for the mount to appear
claims.evidence_quote: the main rclone program will wait for the background mount to become ready or until the timeout specified by the --daemon-wait flag

claims.claim: On Windows the mount is foreground only
claims.evidence_quote: On Windows you can run mount in foreground only, the flag is ignored.

claims.claim: the target can be `*` (auto drive), a drive letter such as `X:`, a path, or a network share
claims.evidence_quote: rclone mount remote:path/to/files * rclone mount remote:path/to/files X: rclone mount remote:path/to/files C:\path\parent\mount rclone mount remote:path/to/files \\cloud\remote

claims.claim: Without `--vfs-cache-mode`, files can only be written sequentially and reads can only seek
claims.evidence_quote: Without the use of --vfs-cache-mode this can only write files sequentially, it can only seek when reading.

claims.claim: so many applications fail; use `writes` or `full`
claims.evidence_quote: This means that many applications won't work with their files on an rclone mount without --vfs-cache-mode writes or --vfs-cache-mode full .

claims.claim: Bucket-based remotes (Azure Blob, Swift, S3, GCS, B2) cannot store empty directories
claims.evidence_quote: Bucket-based remotes - Azure Blob, Swift, S3, Google Cloud Storage and B2 - can't store empty directories.

claims.claim: only Azure Blob, GCS and S3 can keep them with `--xxx-directory_markers`
claims.evidence_quote: Of these, only Azure Blob, Google Cloud Storage and S3 can preserve them when you add --xxx-directory_markers

claims.claim: Filesystems expect reliability that cloud storage lacks
claims.evidence_quote: File systems expect things to be 100% reliable, whereas cloud storage systems are a long way from 100% reliable.

claims.claim: unlike sync and copy, mount cannot retry without local copies of uploads
claims.evidence_quote: The rclone sync/copy commands cope with this with lots of retries. However rclone mount can't use retries in the same way without making local copies of the uploads.

claims.claim: local copies of uploads, which VFS caching provides
claims.evidence_quote: Look at the VFS File Caching for solutions to make mount more reliable.

claims.claim: The service can use `Type=notify`, entering started state after the mount is ready
claims.evidence_quote: it is possible to use Type=notify. In this case the service will enter the started state after the mountpoint has been successfully set up.

claims.claim: systemd gives no `PATH` or `HOME`, so tilde expansion fails: pass `--config` and `--cache-dir` as absolute paths
claims.evidence_quote: This means that tilde ( ~ ) expansion will not work and you should provide --config and --cache-dir explicitly as absolute paths via rclone arguments.

claims.claim: The fallback `PATH` is `/bin:/usr/bin`, which must contain `fusermount` or `fusermount3`
claims.evidence_quote: Since mounting requires the fusermount or fusermount3 program, rclone will use the fallback PATH of /bin:/usr/bin in this scenario. Please ensure that fusermount / fusermount3 is present on this PATH.

claims.claim: Symlink the binary to `/sbin/mount.rclone` (optionally `rclonefs`) and rclone translates mount options
claims.evidence_quote: you should symlink rclone binary to /sbin/mount.rclone and optionally /usr/bin/rclonefs , e.g. ln -s /usr/bin/rclone /sbin/mount.rclone . rclone will detect it and translate command-line arguments appropriately

claims.claim: you can use `mount sftp1:subdir /mnt/data -t rclone -o vfs_cache_mode=writes`
claims.evidence_quote: Now you can run classic mounts like this: mount sftp1:subdir /mnt/data -t rclone -o vfs_cache_mode=writes,sftp_key_file=/path/to/pem

claims.claim: a systemd `.mount` unit with `Type=rclone`, `What=sftp1:subdir` and `Options=rw,_netdev,allow_other,args2env,vfs-cache-mode=writes,config=/etc/rclone.conf,cache-dir=/var/rclone`
claims.evidence_quote: [Mount] Type = rclone What = sftp1:subdir Where = /mnt/data Options = rw,_netdev,allow_other,args2env,vfs-cache-mode=writes,config=/etc/rclone.conf,cache-dir=/var/rclone

claims.claim: On Linux, if AppArmor blocks `fusermount3` you may see "Permission denied"
claims.evidence_quote: fusermount3: mount failed: Permission denied CRITICAL: Fatal error: failed to mount FUSE fs: fusermount: exit status 1 This may be due to newer Apparmor restrictions

claims.claim: On macOS an NFS mount without a cache mode is read-only
claims.evidence_quote: When using NFS mount on macOS, if you don't specify |--vfs-cache-mode| the mount point will be read-only.

coverage: I extracted every command, flag, option value, path, platform list and named behaviour in the skill — the rclone mount invocation, the empty-existing-directory mountpoint rule, the foreground default with Ctrl-C/SIGINT/SIGTERM, --daemon with fusermount -u / fusermount3 -u manual unmount and --daemon-wait, the Windows foreground-only rule and its four mount targets (*, X:, path, network share), the --vfs-cache-mode sequential-write/seek-read limitation with the writes/full recommendation, the bucket-based remote list with --xxx-directory_markers, the sync/copy retry contrast, Type=notify, the PATH/HOME and /bin:/usr/bin fallback facts, --config/--cache-dir absolute paths, the /sbin/mount.rclone and rclonefs symlinks, the mount sftp1:subdir example, the systemd .mount unit options, the AppArmor fusermount3 Permission denied error and the macOS NFS read-only note — and checked each against the single listed source, the rclone mount page, which covers all of them.
